key_findings.title: Bias is a Math Problem, AI Bias is a Technical Problem: 10-year Literature Review of AI/LLM Bias Research Reveals Narrow [Gender-Centric] Conceptions of ‘Bias’, and Academia-Industry Gap
key_findings.summary: Binary gender constructions dominate; 138 papers use binary categories, and 114 explicitly note this as a limitation.

synthesis: A systematic review of 189 AI/LLM bias papers uncovers three interrelated shortcomings. First, the majority (82%) omit explicit definitions of bias, treating it as an abstract technical flaw rather than a socially situated construct. Second, research is overwhelmingly centered on binary gender‑occupation stereotypes, with nearly 80% of studies focusing on gender bias and minimal attention to race, age, religion, or nationality, reflecting dataset constraints and a narrow conceptual lens. Third, only about one in ten papers offer concrete guidance for deploying mitigation strategies, exposing a stark academia‑industry gap that hampers real‑world impact. When bias is defined, it is typically cast as wholly negative, overlooking nuanced or potentially advantageous dimensions. These patterns reveal a field that needs broader, intersectional definitions of bias, diversified evaluation across under‑studied identities, and stronger emphasis on actionable recommendations to bridge scholarly insights with industry practice.
